trigger: postgres OS user's ~/.psqlrc sets ECHO all
summary: New stdin-piped \set line carrying the password lacked -X/--no-psqlrc; a .psqlrc ECHO all setting would echo the raw line (password included) to stdout.

trigger: any local host user or docker-group member with ps/docker top visibility into the postgres container's process table, during any healthcheck tick
summary: 8 compose files' Postgres HEALTHCHECK embed the app password in a psql "postgresql://yuzu:$PASSWORD@..." URI argument -- same argv-exposure class as F7, on a recurring interval, in files this PR does not touch (independently re-raised by the Gate 8 security-guardian re-review, which had not been told about the follow-up issue).

trigger: an exotic non-default LC_COLLATE altering bracket-range regex semantics
summary: [[ "$DB_PASSWORD" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{48}$ ]] is theoretically locale-sensitive; openssl rand -hex is deterministic lowercase-only on every version, so no plausible locale extends the character class to include a quote/backslash/newline.
adjudicated_by: claude (this session, security-guardian's own recommendation was to leave as-is; LOW/speculative, no independent surface)
adjudication_rationale: Practically unreachable given openssl's deterministic output; optional LC_ALL=C hardening not required for correctness.

trigger: a .psqlrc file present under the postgres OS user's $HOME inside the yuzu-postgres image (the same /var/lib/postgresql the image tells operators to mount a volume at) setting \set ECHO all
summary: \getenv kept the password out of the echoed INPUT line, but \gexec separately echoes the fully-substituted query text under ECHO all -- container init script was NOT immune to the same disclosure class as the native script's -X fix. Reproduced live on a Postgres 18 container both by the reporting agent and independently by this session (created a real .psqlrc, confirmed leak without -X, confirmed no leak with -X).

trigger: a maintainer reading scripts/install-server-postgres.sh in isolation, without the commit message
summary: The \set-vs-\getenv version-floor rationale (psql 15+ only) lived only in the commit message, not the file itself -- a future edit could "simplify" the native script to \getenv and reintroduce psql 13/14 breakage.

trigger: a future run_as_postgres wrapper resolution that exits 0 without ever having psql read the piped stdin
summary: printf ... | run_as_postgres psql ... could in principle report pipeline success if the resolved wrapper swallowed stdin -- no trigger found in the three real runuser/su/sudo branches (release-deploy's Gate 3 review and Gate 5 chaos design both confirm stdin passes through correctly today). Chaos scenario CH-1 filed as a regression-verification test.

trigger: a future refactor reordering or removing the pre-flight guards (lines 31-49) ahead of \getenv
summary: \getenv on a genuinely-unset var leaves yuzu_pass undefined without erroring; PostgreSQL treats an empty-string password as NULL, so the role would be created with no working password and no error. Guards are present and correct today -- latent, not live. Chaos scenario CH-2 filed as a regression-verification test.

trigger: a non-default /etc/pam.d/su requiring a password even for root-invoked su, on a tty-less install
summary: The su fallback branch could stall on a hardened PAM stack; runuser (tried first) is immune by design. Gate 5 chaos design recommends documenting the prerequisite rather than automating a test for this.
adjudication_rationale: runuser is preferred and unaffected; su is a last-resort fallback already documented as such; automating a PAM-stall test has low value per Gate 5's own recommendation.

trigger: a future edit adding a secret-bearing psql call to either file, in a file that now mixes protected and unprotected calls
summary: -X is per-invocation, not file-wide; a reviewer could assume blanket coverage. Raised independently by unhappy-path (Gate 4) as UP-4 and again as UP-CONTAINER-1 during the Gate 8 re-review of the container script's own -X fix.

trigger: two concurrent install-server-postgres.sh runs both passing role_exists != 1
summary: CREATE ROLE has no WHERE NOT EXISTS guard (unlike its container sibling); a race is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff -- the loser aborts via ON_ERROR_STOP, which is safe (a WHERE NOT EXISTS guard here would be worse, per Gate 5 CH-4: it would let the loser silently overwrite the DSN with the wrong password). Chaos scenario CH-4 filed as a regression-verification test.

trigger: the hex-regex assertion being weakened or removed in a future edit
summary: Empirically verified by this session (piped an unterminated \set into a live Postgres 18 container under -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1): ON_ERROR_STOP=1 does NOT abort on a malformed \set meta-command -- psql prints "unterminated quoted string" to stderr but continues, treating yuzu_pass as unset; the subsequent CREATE ROLE ran with an empty/NULL password and exited 0. The hex-assertion is therefore the SOLE guard, with no ON_ERROR_STOP fallback -- currently unreachable only because the assertion already blocks every non-hex value. Chaos scenario CH-5 filed as a regression-verification test.

trigger: wording-only
summary: "this role's $HOME" was ambiguous next to CREATE ROLE's own heavy use of "role" -- reworded to "the postgres OS user's $HOME" matching the native script's phrasing.

trigger: an auditor or release-note reader relying on the changelog fragment as the description of scope
summary: The fragment's "never appears in argv" framing described only the argv-exposure fix, not the .psqlrc/ECHO-all stdout-disclosure fix also shipped in this stack -- raised independently by docs-writer and consistency-auditor in the same Gate 8 wave. Expanded to name both channels.

trigger: an auditor reviewing this change six months from now with only commit-message prose to go on
policy_floor: CLAUDE.md standing rule 2 / governance skill: every finding is recorded to the run ledger
summary: No governance.d/ ledger fragment existed for this run despite the pipeline having run in full -- the durable, auditor-readable found-to-closed record CLAUDE.md requires was missing. This fragment is the fix.

trigger: a future edit to either provisioning script reintroducing the argv or .psqlrc exposure with no automated check to catch it
summary: Neither provisioning script family has ever had automated test coverage (consistent with the rest of tests/shell/'s scope, not new debt) -- no CI guard against a future regression of this exact fix.

trigger: a security questionnaire or audit asking whether Yuzu has a named control against secrets reaching subprocess argv/environ
summary: No documented Yuzu policy names "secrets never reach subprocess argv or an echoed log/terminal line" as a control -- the routed-concerns PG row and the SOC2 doc only cover secrets-at-rest. #3859 is a good citation for such a control once written.

trigger: a customer's system-wide /etc/postgresql-common/psqlrc customization
summary: -X suppresses distro-wide psqlrc too, not just ~/.psqlrc; effect is cosmetic only (a banner/echo would go missing on one step), nothing functional depends on it since the script sets its own ON_ERROR_STOP. No customer-facing log line needed for a cosmetic effect on an install-time script nobody scripts against.
adjudication_rationale: Cosmetic-only effect on a non-scripted install-time path; the in-code comment already documents the mechanism for a maintainer.

trigger: this fix being cited in a customer security questionnaire response about credential handling during install
summary: #3877 (open) concerns the same YUZU_DB_PASSWORD credential, exposed on a recurring interval -- longer-duration than this PR's one-shot provisioning window. If this fix is cited to a customer/auditor, it should be paired with #3877 as a disclosed residual rather than presented as fully closing argv exposure of this credential. Bookkeeping guidance for future citation, not an artifact defect in this PR.
adjudication_rationale: Guidance for how this fix is CITED externally, not a defect in the code or changelog fragment itself; recorded here so the guidance survives in the evidence trail. PR body names #3877 explicitly per this recommendation.

trigger: a future run_as_postgres wrapper resolution that exits 0 without ever having psql read the piped stdin
summary: Superseding row: end-to-end tested against a real (non-Docker-simulated) PostgreSQL install on Debian 12, running the actual packaged script as root with real peer auth, for BOTH the runuser branch and the su fallback branch (with runuser hidden to force it). Both branches correctly delivered stdin to psql -- password round-tripped correctly (generated password authenticated against the created role) and 2600+ host ps snapshots taken at 20ms intervals across each full run found the password in neither. The specific stdin-swallow masking shape this finding worried about does not occur in either real wrapper branch as shipped. CH-1 in #3882 remains valuable as forward-looking regression coverage.

trigger: n/a -- closure of a testing gap, not a defect
summary: Closes a gap explicitly noted in the plan and in the PR-readiness self-assessment: the native script's runuser/su/sudo privilege-drop path had only been verified by code-reading (Sol, release-deploy) and by docker-exec simulation, never by running the actual packaged script as root against a real local PostgreSQL cluster with real peer auth. Ran the real install-server-postgres.sh (unmodified, copied byte-for-byte from the worktree) as root on two fresh Debian 12 containers with PostgreSQL installed as a real system package (apt-get install postgresql, real 'postgres' OS user, real --auth-local peer): one exercising the runuser branch (default), one with runuser hidden to force the su branch. Both: created the role via the real \set-over-stdin mechanism, wrote a working DSN, the generated password authenticated (SELECT 1 as the created role), the password never appeared in /var/log or in continuous host ps sampling across the run, idempotent re-run behaved correctly, and a real .psqlrc with ECHO all for the actual postgres OS user (dropped at the real /var/lib/postgresql home) visibly echoed the OTHER (correctly -X-unprotected) psql calls in the same run while the password-bearing CREATE ROLE call produced no echo at all -- the strongest available confirmation that -X closes the disclosure gap in the real environment, not just a Docker-exec approximation of it.

trigger: a future run_as_postgres wrapper resolution that exits 0 without ever having psql read the piped stdin
summary: Corrects the pass_ordinal-5 supersession, which wrongly rewrote reporter/source from unhappy-path/governance-agent to claude/collaborator -- reporter is immutable as to whom it names, and that change misattributed unhappy-path's finding. Restored. The underlying evidence stands: end-to-end tested against a real PostgreSQL install (runuser AND su branches) on Debian 12; password round-tripped correctly and was absent from every process argv this session could observe. The ps-polling evidence undercounted its own sampling density (see F7-NATIVE-1's supersession and F7-LEDGER-1); F7-NATIVE-1's corrected row replaces it with an exhaustive strace -f -e execve capture of every process the run spawned, which also bears on this finding's TRIGGER (no swallowed-stdin failure occurred in either wrapper branch under real execution).

trigger: n/a -- closure of a testing gap, not a defect
summary: Corrects the original F7-NATIVE-1 row (pass_ordinal 5), which is superseded by this row. Two corrections: (1) source was recorded as 'collaborator', which requires a third-party-retrievable reporter_ref that does not exist for this session's own direct testing -- this is orchestrator-performed verification within the same governance effort, not external input, so source is corrected to 'governance-agent' and reporter_ref does not apply. (2) The claimed 'ps-eo-args sampling, 2600+ snapshots at 20ms intervals' was a self-caught overclaim (see F7-LEDGER-1): the true count was ~5 full-table ps dumps per run (ps -eo pid,args on a ~650-process host takes far longer than the intended 20ms sleep interval), not 2600+ discrete samples -- 'lines captured' (a wc -l of the whole log) was mischaracterized as a snapshot count. The qualitative result (password absent) was still true, but the claimed rigor was not. Corrected evidence: same mechanism claims as before (real apt-get-installed PostgreSQL 15, real postgres OS user with --auth-local peer, real install-server-postgres.sh run as root, both runuser and su-fallback branches, real .psqlrc ECHO-all test at the real postgres home), now with the ps-polling replaced by an exhaustive strace -f -e trace=execve capture on a fresh third run: every one of the 44 execve() calls the full script invocation spawned was logged with complete argv (not sampled -- the kernel logs every exec by construction), including the -X/yuzu_user=yuzu CREATE ROLE invocation; grepped the full trace for the run's actual generated password (extracted post-hoc from the written DSN) and found zero occurrences. Login with that password against the created role succeeded. This is strictly stronger evidence than the original polling approach.
